angles: Make the constraints the return engine rather than obstacles: rebalance every trading day by a fixed fraction of the gap between current weights and a risk-budgeted target (exponential partial adjustment). Frequent trading then harvests the rebalancing premium among low-correlation, mean-reverting relative prices (volatility pumping, 'Shannon's demon'), and the adjustment fraction is set analytically so that the worst-case weekly turnover stays at or below 20% whatever the gap. The signal changes where the target sits, never how fast the portfolio is allowed to chase it.

Treat the 20% drawdown limit as a consumable budget that is part of the portfolio's state: risky exposure is a function of the remaining headroom to a floor that ratchets up with the high-water mark. That is paired with a correlation-regime detector computed from closing prices (the average pairwise 60-day correlation, or the share of variance in the first eigenvalue) that shrinks the headroom multiplier before diversification fails in a correlated sell-off. The worst-case drawdown can then be argued as a bound: headroom multiplied by an assumed gap-down size, plus the lag imposed by the turnover cap, rather than estimated from history.

domains.text: Reservoir operation under drought 'hedging rules': operators ration releases progressively as storage falls through rule-curve zones instead of releasing at full demand until empty, and they obey limits on how fast releases may ramp and on minimum flows each day. This maps to drawdown-zone de-risking under a turnover cap that limits the rate of change.

Closed-loop insulin delivery (the artificial pancreas): a controller doses in small increments every few minutes under hard limits on the delivery rate, and it tracks 'insulin on board' (committed action that has not yet taken effect) so that it does not overshoot into hypoglycaemia. This maps to rate-limited daily trading toward a target with an explicit account of adjustments still pending under the turnover budget.
